under400.label: 400 分以下
under400.description: 基礎句型、常見字彙、時間地點、be/do/have 與簡單職場情境

questions.prompt: The customer ___ the order by phone yesterday.
questions.explanation: “Yesterday” calls for the simple past: placed.

questions.prompt: Please arrive ___ 8:30 a.m. for the staff meeting.
questions.explanation: A specific clock time takes the preposition “at.”

questions.prompt: Ms. Chen is responsible ___ checking the inventory.
questions.explanation: The fixed pattern is “be responsible for + -ing/noun.”

questions.prompt: The office is closed ___ Sundays.
questions.explanation: Days of the week take “on.”

questions.prompt: We need ___ copies of the new brochure.
questions.explanation: “Copies” is countable plural, so “a few” fits.

questions.prompt: The train leaves at 9:10, so please be ___ the station by 9:00.
questions.explanation: “Be at + place” is the natural location pattern.

questions.prompt: Mr. Lee ___ the report every Friday.
questions.explanation: A regular habit with a singular subject takes present simple “sends.”

questions.prompt: The receptionist asked visitors to ___ their names.
questions.explanation: “Ask someone to + base verb” is correct.

questions.prompt: The meeting room is ___ the second floor.
questions.explanation: Floors use “on”: on the second floor.

questions.prompt: Please ___ the attached form before noon.
questions.explanation: After “please,” use the base verb “complete.”

questions.prompt: We have two printers, but ___ is out of order.
questions.explanation: “One” refers to one of two known printers.

questions.prompt: The manager will call you ___ the afternoon.
questions.explanation: Parts of the day use “in”: in the afternoon.

questions.prompt: Our store opens ___ 10 a.m. every weekday.
questions.explanation: A specific time uses “at.”

questions.prompt: The package was delivered ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: Specific days use “on.”

questions.prompt: The new employee is very ___ with customers.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed after “is very.”

questions.prompt: There ___ three chairs in the waiting area.
questions.explanation: “Three chairs” is plural, so use “are.”

questions.prompt: We need to finish the work ___ Friday.
questions.explanation: “By Friday” means no later than Friday.

questions.prompt: Mr. Park is ___ engineer at the company.
questions.explanation: “Engineer” begins with a vowel sound, so use “an.”

questions.prompt: The receptionist gave the visitor a ___ pass.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun “pass.”

questions.prompt: The store closes at six, ___ customers usually leave earlier.
questions.explanation: “But” introduces a contrast with the first clause.

400-600.description: 常見時態、被動、職場搭配、基本從句與條件句

questions.prompt: Because the shipment arrived late, the warehouse team ___ the delivery schedule.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a completed response to a past event, so “revised” fits.

questions.prompt: All employees must submit their travel receipts ___ ten days of returning.
questions.explanation: “Within ten days” means no later than ten days after return.

questions.prompt: The new software was ___ last Monday and is now available to all staff.
questions.explanation: The passive form is “was installed.”

questions.prompt: Ms. Gomez has worked at the branch ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: “Since” is used with a starting point in time.

questions.prompt: The director asked whether the conference room ___ available.
questions.explanation: After “asked whether,” the past form “was” fits the reported context.

questions.prompt: Please make sure that every invoice ___ correctly before payment.
questions.explanation: A passive form is required because invoices receive the action.

questions.prompt: The sales team is looking forward to ___ the new clients next week.
questions.explanation: “Look forward to” is followed by a gerund.

questions.prompt: The company delayed the launch ___ several parts were not ready.
questions.explanation: “Because” explains the reason for the delay.

questions.prompt: The technician will replace the battery if the test ___ a defect.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional, the if-clause uses present simple.

questions.prompt: The training session, ___ was originally scheduled for Tuesday, has been moved to Friday.
questions.explanation: “Which” introduces a nonrestrictive relative clause referring to the session.

questions.prompt: Our supplier offered a discount ___ we ordered more than 500 units.
questions.explanation: “If” introduces the condition for receiving the discount.

questions.prompt: The manager reminded staff ___ their passwords every 90 days.
questions.explanation: “Remind someone to do something” is the correct pattern.

questions.prompt: By the time the guests arrived, the staff ___ all the tables.
questions.explanation: The earlier past action takes past perfect: “had set.”

questions.prompt: The marketing report provides useful information ___ customer preferences.
questions.explanation: “Information about” is the standard collocation.

questions.prompt: We cannot issue the refund until the returned item ___.
questions.explanation: The item receives the inspection, so passive is needed.

questions.prompt: The applicant has experience ___ international clients.
questions.explanation: “Experience + -ing” is natural in this context.

questions.prompt: The memo explains ___ employees should follow the new procedure.
questions.explanation: “Explains how employees should…” introduces the manner/procedure.

questions.prompt: If you have any questions, please ___ the customer service desk.
questions.explanation: After “please,” use the base verb.

questions.prompt: The company has reduced costs ___ switching to digital invoices.
questions.explanation: “By + -ing” expresses the method used to achieve a result.

questions.prompt: The office will remain closed ___ the electrical inspection is complete.
questions.explanation: “Until” identifies the point when the office will reopen.

600-800.description: 較長句型、職場語境、子句、連接語意、推論與高階文法控制

questions.prompt: The revised policy takes effect next month, at which point all regional offices ___ the same reporting procedure.
questions.explanation: The future reference “next month” requires future “will adopt.”

questions.prompt: The consultant recommended that the company ___ its vendor approval process.
questions.explanation: After a formal recommendation, the mandative subjunctive uses the base form “streamline.”

questions.prompt: The proposal was rejected, not because it was too expensive, ___ because its timetable was unrealistic.
questions.explanation: The correlative structure is “not because…, but because…”.

questions.prompt: The board approved the expansion plan, ___ several directors had raised concerns about staffing.
questions.explanation: “Even though” expresses contrast with the approval.

questions.prompt: The report is intended to provide managers with data ___ they can use when allocating resources.
questions.explanation: “That” introduces a relative clause modifying “data.”

questions.prompt: Only after the final audit ___ the accounting team release the figures.
questions.explanation: After fronted negative/restrictive adverbials, subject–auxiliary inversion is required.

questions.prompt: The conference was postponed because the keynote speaker was delayed, ___ left organizers with little time to revise the program.
questions.explanation: “Which” refers to the preceding situation.

questions.prompt: The merger could generate significant savings, provided that the two companies ___ their procurement systems.
questions.explanation: “Provided that” takes a present form for a future condition.

questions.prompt: The analyst noted that the decline in sales was less severe than ___ initially anticipated.
questions.explanation: “Than what was initially anticipated” uses a noun clause as the comparison object.

questions.prompt: The memo says the new platform is easier to use, but several employees report that it is no more intuitive than the one it ___.
questions.explanation: The relative clause refers to the current platform’s replacement relation; present simple fits a general fact.

questions.prompt: Had the supplier notified us earlier, we ___ able to arrange an alternative shipment.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional inversion: “Had + past participle…, would have + participle.”

questions.prompt: The training materials should be concise enough for new hires to understand them without ___ assistance.
questions.explanation: An adjective modifying “assistance” is required.

questions.prompt: The committee will publish the findings once the legal team ___ the wording.
questions.explanation: After “once” for a future event, use present simple.

questions.prompt: Applicants whose references cannot be verified may be asked ___ additional documentation.
questions.explanation: “Ask someone to do something” requires the infinitive.

questions.prompt: The software upgrade is expected to improve security without ___ system performance.
questions.explanation: After the preposition “without,” use the gerund.

questions.prompt: The report highlights three areas in which the company could improve, the first of ___ is staff training.
questions.explanation: “The first of which” is the standard relative construction.

questions.prompt: The manager was reluctant to approve the purchase until she had confirmed that the equipment met all regulatory ___.
questions.explanation: “Regulatory requirements” is the correct noun phrase.

questions.prompt: The hotel has introduced a digital check-in service, thereby ___ waiting times for guests.
questions.explanation: “Thereby + -ing” expresses the resulting method/action.

questions.prompt: The author argues that productivity depends less on the number of hours worked than on how effectively those hours ___.
questions.explanation: The hours receive the action, so passive “are used” is needed.

questions.prompt: The committee requested that all proposals ___ submitted in both digital and printed form.
questions.explanation: After “requested that,” the formal mandative subjunctive uses “be.”

800-990.description: 正式語域、倒裝、精準搭配、複雜從句、推論與高階語法控制

questions.prompt: Rarely ___ a supplier respond so quickly to a complex compliance request.
questions.explanation: Fronted negative adverb “rarely” triggers inversion: “do we see.”

questions.prompt: The legal department advised that the contract be amended to avoid any ambiguity ___ the termination clause.
questions.explanation: “Concerning” functions as a preposition meaning “about.”

questions.prompt: The acquisition would be viable only if projected savings were realized and integration costs ___ within budget.
questions.explanation: A parallel second condition in the hypothetical frame takes simple past “remained.”

questions.prompt: The report is worth reading in full, particularly the section ___ the assumptions underlying the forecast.
questions.explanation: “The section concerning…” is the most concise grammatical noun phrase.

questions.prompt: What the committee found most troubling ___ not the delay itself but the lack of communication that followed.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun clause “What the committee found most troubling.”

questions.prompt: The director denied that the figures had been deliberately understated, a claim that was later ___ by the audit findings.
questions.explanation: “Bear out” means confirm or support with evidence.

questions.prompt: The revised forecast assumes that demand will remain stable; ___, however, it would be prudent to retain sufficient capacity for a surge.
questions.explanation: “Nevertheless” signals a contrast with the assumption.

questions.prompt: No sooner ___ the announcement been made than investors began asking about the financing arrangement.
questions.explanation: “No sooner had … than …” uses past perfect inversion.

questions.prompt: The consultant's recommendation was more nuanced than the summary initially made ___.
questions.explanation: Causative “make + object + bare infinitive” gives “made it appear.”

questions.prompt: Were the regulator to reject the application, the company ___ required to resubmit the entire package.
questions.explanation: Formal second conditional inversion: “Were …, would …”.

questions.prompt: The CEO's remarks were carefully worded so as to avoid ___ the impression that the merger was imminent.
questions.explanation: “Avoid” is followed by a gerund: avoiding creating.

questions.prompt: The policy applies to all contractors, regardless of where they are based or ___ long they have worked with the company.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is “how long.”

questions.prompt: The figures are consistent with the hypothesis, but they are by no means ___ evidence of causation.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before “evidence”: conclusive evidence.

questions.prompt: Under no circumstances ___ confidential client records be shared with external parties without authorization.
questions.explanation: “Under no circumstances” triggers inversion; “should … be shared” expresses prohibition/policy.

questions.prompt: The report distinguishes between what the market appears to be doing and what analysts believe it ___.
questions.explanation: Future-oriented “will do” completes the contrast.

questions.prompt: The new framework is designed to be flexible enough to accommodate changes that could not reasonably ___ when the original policy was drafted.
questions.explanation: A modal perfect passive is required for an unrealized past possibility.

questions.prompt: Far from ___ the issue, the announcement raised a new set of questions about implementation.
questions.explanation: “Far from + -ing” introduces a contrastive result.

questions.prompt: The auditor's findings call into question the extent to ___ management's estimates can be relied.
questions.explanation: The fixed construction is “the extent to which.”

questions.prompt: It is essential that the final figures ___ independently verified before publication.
questions.explanation: Formal mandative subjunctive uses the bare form “be.”

questions.prompt: The policy, though broadly supported, leaves unresolved the question of ___ liability should be assigned when data are breached.
questions.explanation: “Whose liability” correctly asks about ownership/responsibility.
